name: @dropl/mcp

tools.name: whoami
tools.description: Shows the connected Dropl account, user, role, and API key (name, prefix, scopes, site restriction) plus the web app URL. Use it first in a session to confirm which account you're acting on, or when another tool reports a sign-in or permission error. Needs a saved sign-in or DROPL_API_KEY; it never returns the full key.

tools.name: list_sites
tools.description: Lists the client sites (one per client website) this connection can reach, with their domains and the plan's site allowance. Use it before creating anything, to find the site id for the client the user means and avoid duplicate sites. Keys restricted to some sites only see those sites.

tools.name: create_site
tools.description: Creates a client site: the home for one client website's showcases, videos, collections, and feedback. Use it when the client has no site yet; check list_sites first to avoid duplicates. Only call after showing the plan to the user and getting explicit confirmation. Counts toward the plan's site allowance; safe to retry, since the same name and domain return the same site.

name.description: Client or website name, e.g. "Acme Builders".

domain.description: The website's hostname, e.g. "acme.com" (a pasted URL like https://www.acme.com/ also works).

tools.name: list_showcases
tools.description: Lists a client site's showcases (embeddable photo and video galleries), newest first, with item counts. Use it to reuse an existing gallery instead of creating a duplicate, or to find a showcase id. Paged: pass nextCursor to get more.

siteId.description: Client site id from list_sites, e.g. "0190f5c2-7b1e-7c3a-9d2f-1a2b3c4d5e6f".

cursor.description: nextCursor from a previous call, e.g. "eyJpZCI6IjAxOTAifQ".

tools.name: create_showcase
tools.description: Creates a showcase: an embeddable photo/video gallery the client can update from their phone. Use it when the user wants a gallery, portfolio, project photos, or a section the client can update themselves. Requires a site id from list_sites or create_site. Only call after showing the plan to the user and getting explicit confirmation. Turn on showCategoryFilters when items will be grouped into categories. Safe to retry with the same arguments.

siteId.description: Client site id from list_sites or create_site, e.g. "0190f5c2-7b1e-7c3a-9d2f-1a2b3c4d5e6f".

gridFit.description: cover crops grid tiles; contain letterboxes them to show the whole item, e.g. "cover".

showCategoryFilters.description: Show category filter tabs above the items, e.g. true when items are grouped into categories.

pageSize.description: Items per "Load more" page (3–100), or null to show everything, e.g. 12.

tools.name: get_showcase
tools.description: Summarizes a showcase: settings, item counts by status (processing/ready/failed) and kind, categories with counts, photos without alt text, and failed items. Use it to check that an upload finished processing or to review a gallery before changing it. It returns counts, not items: use list_showcase_items for ids, alt text, and categories.

showcaseId.description: Showcase id from list_showcases or create_showcase, e.g. "0190f5c2-7b1e-7c3a-9d2f-1a2b3c4d5e6f".

tools.name: list_showcase_items
tools.description: Pages through a showcase's items in display order: id, kind, status, file name, the local path it was uploaded from, alt text, and categories. Use it to find item ids for update_items or tag_items, or photos that still need alt text (missingAlt: true). Up to 200 items per call; local paths only appear for files uploaded from this machine.

kind.description: Only photos or only videos, e.g. "photo".

missingAlt.description: Only photos without alt text, e.g. true.

category.description: Only items in this category (name, slug, or id), e.g. "Kitchens".

search.description: Case-insensitive text in the file name, local path, or alt text, e.g. "deck".

offset.description: nextOffset from a previous call, e.g. 50.

tools.name: update_items
tools.description: Sets alt text and adds/removes categories on many showcase items in one call. Use it after an upload to fix alt text or categories by id (files[].id from upload_photos / upload_videos, library video ids, or ids from list_showcase_items) instead of uploading again. Up to 1000 items per call; category names that don't exist yet are created. Alt text: Write concise, descriptive alt text: what the photo shows (e.g. "Cedar deck with glass railing at dusk"), without "image of" or "photo of". Leave it empty for purely decorative photos. Show the user the alt text you plan to write before saving a large batch.

id.description: Item id (or a library video id in this showcase), e.g. "0190f5c2-7b1e-7c3a-9d2f-1a2b3c4d5e6f".

alt.description: New alt text, e.g. "Cedar deck with glass railing at dusk"; empty or null clears it (decorative photo). Omit to leave it unchanged.

addCategories.description: Category names, slugs, or ids to add, e.g. ["Decks"].

removeCategories.description: Category names, slugs, or ids to remove, e.g. ["Uncategorized"].

items.description: Changes per item, e.g. [{ "id": "…", "alt": "Stone patio with fire pit", "addCategories": ["Patios"] }].

tools.name: update_showcase
tools.description: Changes a showcase's title, layout, grid fit, category filter tabs, or items per page. Use it when the user wants the gallery to look or page differently; embeds pick up the change without new code. Pass only the settings to change; at least one is required.

gridFit.description: cover crops grid tiles; contain letterboxes them to show the whole item, e.g. "cover".

showCategoryFilters.description: Show category filter tabs above the items, e.g. true when items are grouped into categories.

pageSize.description: Items per "Load more" page (3–100), or null to show everything, e.g. 12.

tools.name: create_category
tools.description: Adds a category (a filter tab) to a showcase. Use it to group items, e.g. one category per project type or source folder, before tagging them; upload and tagging tools also create missing categories by name. If one with the same name or slug exists, it's returned instead of creating a duplicate.

slug.description: URL form, e.g. "kitchen-remodels"; derived from the name if omitted.

tools.name: tag_items
tools.description: Adds and/or removes the same categories on many showcase items (photos or videos) at once. Use it to put uploaded items into filter tabs, with itemIds from upload_photos / upload_videos (files[].id; library video ids work too) or list_showcase_items. Up to 1000 items per call; category names that don't exist yet are created. For per-item changes or alt text, use update_items.

itemIds.description: Item ids (files[].id from uploads, or from list_showcase_items), e.g. ["0190f5c2-7b1e-7c3a-9d2f-1a2b3c4d5e6f"].

addCategoryIds.description: Existing category ids to add, e.g. ["0190f5c2-7b1e-7c3a-9d2f-1a2b3c4d5e6f"].

addCategoryNames.description: Category names to add, created if missing, e.g. ["Decks", "Patios"].

tools.name: upload_photos
tools.description: Uploads local photos (JPEG, PNG, WebP, AVIF, HEIC; up to 20 MB each) into a showcase, straight to storage. Use it to turn a folder of project photos into a client-editable gallery: pass files, folders (recursive by default), and globs via paths, and per-photo alt text and categories via files. Skips hidden files and validates file contents. Run with dryRun: true first and show the result to the user; Only call after showing the plan to the user and getting explicit confirmation. Resumable: re-running with the same arguments skips files already uploaded (and still applies changed alt text and categories). categoryFromFolder tags each photo with its top-level folder's name; categories tags every photo (both created if missing). Returns files: each local path with its showcase item id and status, for update_items and tag_items. Alt text: Write concise, descriptive alt text: what the photo shows (e.g. "Cedar deck with glass railing at dusk"), without "image of" or "photo of". Leave it empty for purely decorative photos.

showcaseId.description: Showcase id from create_showcase or list_showcases, e.g. "0190f5c2-7b1e-7c3a-9d2f-1a2b3c4d5e6f".

paths.description: Files, folders, or glob patterns, e.g. ["/abs/photos/**/*.jpg"]. Prefer absolute paths; relative ones resolve against cwd. Pass paths, files, or both.

files.description: Photos with their own alt text and categories, e.g. [{ "path": "/abs/photos/deck.jpg", "alt": "Cedar deck at dusk", "categories": ["Decks"] }].

path.description: A photo file (or a folder/glob, applying the same alt text and categories to each), e.g. "/abs/photos/deck.jpg".

alt.description: Alt text, up to 500 characters, e.g. "Cedar deck with glass railing at dusk". Empty or null for a purely decorative photo; omit to leave it unchanged.

categories.description: Categories for this photo (created if missing), e.g. ["Decks"].

cwd.description: Absolute path of the user's project folder; relative paths resolve against it, e.g. "/Users/ana/sites/acme".

recursive.description: Include subfolders (default true), e.g. false to upload only the top folder.

categoryFromFolder.description: Tag photos with their top-level folder name as a category (default false), e.g. true for Kitchens/ and Decks/ folders.

categories.description: Category names to tag every uploaded photo with, e.g. ["Featured"].

dryRun.description: Only check the files and report what would be uploaded, e.g. true for the first call.

tools.name: list_videos
tools.description: Lists videos in a client site's library (newest first), optionally filtered by a title search. Use it to find video ids for get_embed_code or add_videos_to_showcase, or to check a video is already hosted before uploading it again. Paged: pass nextCursor for more.

siteId.description: Client site id from list_sites, e.g. "0190f5c2-7b1e-7c3a-9d2f-1a2b3c4d5e6f".

search.description: Text in the video title, e.g. "hero".

cursor.description: nextCursor from a previous call, e.g. "eyJpZCI6IjAxOTAifQ".

tools.name: upload_videos
tools.description: Uploads local videos (MP4, MOV, WebM, MKV, AVI, MPEG, M4V) to a client site's video library in resumable parts, titled from their file names, for streaming playback without YouTube or Vimeo. Use it to host a hero video or a folder of clips; with showcaseId it also adds them to that showcase (and applies categories / categoryFromFolder). Run with dryRun: true first; Only call after showing the plan to the user and getting explicit confirmation. Re-running with the same arguments resumes interrupted uploads and skips finished ones. Returns files: each local path with its library video id.

siteId.description: Client site id from list_sites, e.g. "0190f5c2-7b1e-7c3a-9d2f-1a2b3c4d5e6f".

paths.description: Files, folders, or glob patterns, e.g. ["/abs/photos/**/*.jpg"]. Prefer absolute paths; relative ones resolve against cwd.

cwd.description: Absolute path of the user's project folder; relative paths resolve against it, e.g. "/Users/ana/sites/acme".

recursive.description: Include subfolders (default true), e.g. false to upload only the top folder.

showcaseId.description: Showcase (in the same site) to add the videos to, e.g. "0190f5c2-7b1e-7c3a-9d2f-1a2b3c4d5e6f".

categoryFromFolder.description: With showcaseId: tag each video with its top-level folder name, e.g. true.

categories.description: With showcaseId: categories to tag every video with, e.g. ["Tours"].

dryRun.description: Only check the files and report what would be uploaded, e.g. true for the first call.

tools.name: add_videos_to_showcase
tools.description: Adds existing library videos to a showcase. Use it for videos already hosted in Dropl (ids from list_videos or upload_videos) instead of uploading them again. Videos must belong to the showcase's client site; ones already in it are skipped.

videoIds.description: Library video ids from list_videos or upload_videos, e.g. ["0190f5c2-7b1e-7c3a-9d2f-1a2b3c4d5e6f"].

tools.name: get_embed_code
tools.description: Returns the official embed snippet for a video (videoId) or a showcase (showcaseId, optionally one category by name or slug), plus where and how to paste it (plain HTML, React/Next.js, WordPress, Webflow, Framer). Use it whenever a gallery or video goes onto a page. Always use this instead of writing embed HTML by hand; pass exactly one of videoId or showcaseId.

videoId.description: Video id from list_videos or upload_videos, e.g. "0190f5c2-7b1e-7c3a-9d2f-1a2b3c4d5e6f".

category.description: With showcaseId: a category name or slug, to embed only that category without filter tabs, e.g. "kitchens".

tools.name: get_usage
tools.description: Shows storage and bandwidth used against the plan's limits this period, and whether uploads or playback are suspended. Use it before a large upload, or when the user asks how much space is left. Figures cover the whole account, not one client site.

tools.name: plan_migration
tools.description: Scans a local folder without uploading and proposes how to bring it into Dropl: top-level folders become categories, photo/video counts and sizes per folder, unsupported files by reason, upload batches, whether it needs several showcases, remaining storage, and the tool calls to run. Use it first for any folder-to-gallery move or site migration, then show the plan to the user for confirmation. Works offline; remaining storage is only included when signed in.

path.description: Folder to scan; prefer an absolute path, e.g. "/Users/ana/sites/acme/public/projects".

cwd.description: Absolute path of the user's project folder; relative paths resolve against it, e.g. "/Users/ana/sites/acme".

recursive.description: Include subfolders (default true), e.g. false to upload only the top folder.

categoryFromFolder.description: Turn top-level folders into categories (default true), e.g. false for one flat gallery.

tools.name: list_collections
tools.description: Lists a client site's collections (menus, inventory, events, …) with item counts, when a website last read each one, and the plan's item and collection limits. Use it to find a collection id (a menu, inventory, team, or events) before reading or changing one, and to reuse an existing collection instead of creating a duplicate. Trashed collections only appear with trashed: true.

trashed.description: List trashed collections instead (restorable for 30 days), e.g. true.

tools.name: get_collection_schema
tools.description: Reads a collection's current fields, schemaVersion, and site time zone, including edits made in the dashboard. Always call this before planning a change and pass its schemaVersion as expectedSchemaVersion. Use it right before any change to a collection or its items, since clients and teammates edit in the dashboard. It returns the schemaVersion that plan_collections needs to change an existing collection.

tools.name: plan_collections
tools.description: Dry run: previews creating or changing up to 10 collections on a client site and returns a plain-text diff (fields added, renamed, removed, items affected). Nothing is saved. Use it whenever the user wants content their client can edit (a menu, inventory, events, team) or a field change; nothing is saved. Show the summary to the user before apply_collection_plan.

slug.description: Matches an existing collection of the site; otherwise a new one gets this slug, e.g. "menu".

description.description: Shown to clients in the dashboard, e.g. "Dishes on the dinner menu."

templateKey.description: Start a new collection from a template when fields are omitted, e.g. "menu".

key.description: Existing fields: always send their current key (from get_collection_schema), e.g. "price". New fields: omit; it's derived from the label.

helpText.description: Hint under the field, e.g. "Leave empty for market price."

required.description: Whether every item needs a value, e.g. true.

value.description: Stored value, e.g. "vegan"; derived from the label when omitted. Keep existing values unchanged.

min.description: number, price (amount), or text length minimum, e.g. 0.

max.description: number, price (amount), or text length maximum, e.g. 100.

titleFieldKey.description: Key of the field shown as each item's title, e.g. "name".

visibility.description: public (default) can be read by the website without a key, e.g. "public".

expectedSchemaVersion.description: Required to change an existing collection: the schemaVersion you read with get_collection_schema, e.g. 3.

collections.description: Collections to create or change, e.g. [{ "name": "Menu", "fields": [{ "label": "Name", "type": "text" }, { "label": "Price", "type": "price", "currency": "USD" }] }].

tools.name: apply_collection_plan
tools.description: Creates or changes the collections previewed with plan_collections. Destructive changes are refused unless confirmDestructive is true, and a collection edited since its expectedSchemaVersion is refused as a conflict. Use it with exactly the collections you passed to plan_collections, once the user approved that plan. Only call after showing the plan to the user and getting explicit confirmation.

slug.description: Matches an existing collection of the site; otherwise a new one gets this slug, e.g. "menu".

description.description: Shown to clients in the dashboard, e.g. "Dishes on the dinner menu."

templateKey.description: Start a new collection from a template when fields are omitted, e.g. "menu".

key.description: Existing fields: always send their current key (from get_collection_schema), e.g. "price". New fields: omit; it's derived from the label.

helpText.description: Hint under the field, e.g. "Leave empty for market price."

required.description: Whether every item needs a value, e.g. true.

value.description: Stored value, e.g. "vegan"; derived from the label when omitted. Keep existing values unchanged.

min.description: number, price (amount), or text length minimum, e.g. 0.

max.description: number, price (amount), or text length maximum, e.g. 100.

titleFieldKey.description: Key of the field shown as each item's title, e.g. "name".

visibility.description: public (default) can be read by the website without a key, e.g. "public".

expectedSchemaVersion.description: Required to change an existing collection: the schemaVersion you read with get_collection_schema, e.g. 3.

collections.description: Collections to create or change, e.g. [{ "name": "Menu", "fields": [{ "label": "Name", "type": "text" }, { "label": "Price", "type": "price", "currency": "USD" }] }].

confirmDestructive.description: Only after the user explicitly agreed to every destructive change in the plan, e.g. true.

tools.name: add_collection_items
tools.description: Bulk-adds items to a collection with per-item errors keyed by field key. Use it to move a hard-coded list (a menu array in a component, rows from a CSV) into a collection. Run with dryRun: true (the default) first; saving (dryRun: false) needs explicit confirmation. Accepts up to 2000 items, sent in batches; retrying the same call doesn't duplicate items.

values.description: Values keyed by field key (see get_collection_schema), e.g. { "name": "Margherita", "price": 14 }.

slug.description: URL form of the item, e.g. "margherita".

dryRun.description: Validate only (default true), e.g. false to save after the user confirmed.

mode.description: valid_only (default) saves the valid items; all_or_nothing saves nothing if any item is invalid, e.g. "all_or_nothing".

tools.name: list_collection_items
tools.description: Lists a collection's items, drafts included, with search, status and field filters, sorting, and paging. Use it to check what's already in a collection before importing, or to find items. Up to 100 items per call; page with offset.

q.description: Search titles and text fields, e.g. "pizza".

status.description: Only drafts or only published items, e.g. "published".

operator.description: eq (default) matches any of comma-separated values, e.g. "eq".

sort.description: position (default), createdAt, updatedAt, publishedAt, title, or a field key; prefix - for descending, e.g. "-updatedAt".

trashed.description: List trashed items instead, e.g. true.

offset.description: Items to skip, e.g. 50 for the second page of 50.

tools.name: get_collection_code
tools.description: Returns TypeScript types and a Next.js fetch example generated from the collection's current fields, plus its public items URL. Use this instead of guessing the response shape. Use it when wiring a page to read a collection, instead of guessing the response shape. Only published items reach the website.

tools.name: undo_collection_change
tools.description: Undoes the most recent schema change of a collection (or the given activity entry) when no data written since would be lost. Use it when the user wants to revert a field or collection change. Only call after showing the plan to the user and getting explicit confirmation.

activityId.description: Activity entry to undo; defaults to the most recent undoable one, e.g. "0190f5c2-7b1e-7c3a-9d2f-1a2b3c4d5e6f".

tools.name: list_feedback
tools.description: Lists feedback the client left on their website (comments on elements, text changes, general notes), newest first. Use it when the user asks to fix, review, or triage client feedback or change requests. Defaults to open and in progress. Text changes (type text_change) give the current and the exact new wording; they can usually be applied directly in the code (search the project for currentText). Use get_feedback for the full context of one request.

status.description: Defaults to open and in_progress, e.g. ["done"].

type.description: Only one kind of request, e.g. "text_change".

page.description: Only requests on pages whose path contains this, e.g. "/menu".

offset.description: Requests to skip, e.g. 20 for the second page of 20.

tools.name: get_feedback
tools.description: Gets one feedback request with its full context: page URL, the clicked element (CSS selector, tag, nearby text, position), device and viewport, screenshot and photo URLs, and the thread. Use it before changing code for a request. Text changes (type text_change) give the current and the exact new wording; they can usually be applied directly in the code (search the project for currentText). If a request is ambiguous, reply_to_feedback asking the client to clarify instead of guessing. Screenshot and photo URLs are temporary; fetch them to look.

tools.name: reply_to_feedback
tools.description: Replies in a feedback request's thread as the signed-in user; the client gets the reply by email. Use it to ask the client to clarify, or to tell them what changed. If a request is ambiguous, reply_to_feedback asking the client to clarify instead of guessing. Keep replies short and plain (no code). Safe to retry: the same reply isn't posted twice.

message.description: The reply, e.g. "Should the new hours apply to both locations?".

tools.name: update_feedback_status
tools.description: Sets a feedback request to open, in_progress, done, or wont_do. Use it after fixing a request (done) or deciding not to (wont_do). After fixing a request, mark it done with update_feedback_status and a short note saying what changed (the client gets it by email). Marking done emails the client; only mark done once the fix is in the code (and deployed, if the user says so).

resolutionNote.description: Short note for done or wont_do, e.g. "Updated the opening hours on the contact page."

instructions:
Dropl hosts client-editable photo and video galleries (showcases), videos, and collections that web studios embed on their clients' websites; clients then update them from the Dropl dashboard or their phone, without a CMS. These tools set that up from the user's codebase: create client sites and showcases, upload local photos and videos, fetch embed code, manage collections, and work through client feedback. Typical flow: whoami, then list_sites (or create_site), create_showcase, upload_photos, and get_embed_code, then paste the embed and build. Before creating or uploading anything, show the user the plan and wait for their explicit confirmation.

Rules:
- Before creating a site or showcase or uploading anything, run plan_migration (or upload_photos / upload_videos with dryRun: true), show the plan to the user (client site, showcase title, categories, file counts and sizes) and get their explicit confirmation. Don't create or upload on your own initiative.
- Prefer existing client sites and showcases (list_sites, list_showcases) over creating duplicates.
- Never ask the user to paste an API key into the chat. If a tool says you're not signed in, ask the user to run `npx -y @dropl/mcp login` in their own terminal (or set DROPL_API_KEY in this server's MCP config), then try again.
- Pass absolute paths (or set cwd to the project folder) for uploads.
- Uploads are resumable and idempotent: if one stops partway, run the same call again; finished files are skipped.
- Uploads return each file's id (files[].id); use those ids with update_items or tag_items instead of re-uploading. list_showcase_items pages through every item with its local path, alt text, and categories.
- Alt text: Write concise, descriptive alt text: what the photo shows (e.g. "Cedar deck with glass railing at dusk"), without "image of" or "photo of". Leave it empty for purely decorative photos. Set it per photo with upload_photos files[].alt, or later with update_items.
- Use get_embed_code for embed snippets; never write embed HTML by hand.
- After adding an embed to the user's project, run the project's build (or type check) to make sure it still compiles.

Collections (structured content like menus, inventory, and events that clients edit in the dashboard):
- Always read the current fields with get_collection_schema before changing a collection. Clients and teammates edit in the dashboard, so your earlier copy may be stale. Never revert or overwrite their edits.
- Run plan_collections first (it never saves), show the summary to the user, and only call apply_collection_plan after their explicit confirmation. Pass confirmDestructive: true only after they agree to every change marked destructive.
- Keep existing field keys and option values exactly; rename only labels. Websites read the keys.
- Import items with add_collection_items and dryRun: true first; fix or report per-item errors before saving.
- Use get_collection_code for the website's TypeScript types and fetch code instead of guessing the response shape. Only published items reach the website.

Feedback (requests clients leave on their website). To fix the open Dropl feedback:
1. list_sites to find the site, then list_feedback (open and in progress by default).
2. get_feedback for each request: page, element selector and nearby text, device, screenshot, and the thread.
3. Text changes (type text_change) give the current and the exact new wording; they can usually be applied directly in the code (search the project for currentText).
4. If a request is ambiguous, reply_to_feedback asking the client to clarify instead of guessing.
5. After fixing a request, mark it done with update_feedback_status and a short note saying what changed (the client gets it by email).
Tell the user which requests you fixed, which you asked about, and which you skipped.
